library(gt) library(dplyr) reactions_mini <- reactions |> filter(cmpd_type == "mercaptan") |> select(cmpd_name, cmpd_formula, ends_with("k298")) |> mutate(cmpd_formula = paste0("%", cmpd_formula, "%")) reactions_mini |> gt(rowname_col = "cmpd_name") |> tab_header(title = "Gas-phase reactions of selected mercaptan compounds") |> tab_spanner( columns = ends_with("k298"), label = md("Reaction Rate Constant (298 K),
{{cm^3 molecules^–1 s^–1}}") ) |> fmt_units(columns = cmpd_formula) |> fmt_scientific(columns = ends_with("k298")) |> sub_missing() |> cols_hide(columns = O3_k298) |> cols_label( cmpd_formula = "", OH_k298 = "OH", NO3_k298 = "{{%NO3%}}", Cl_k298 = "Cl" ) |> opt_stylize(style = 1, color = "blue") |> opt_horizontal_padding(scale = 3) |> opt_table_font(stack = "humanist")

nano_opts <-
  nanoplot_options(
    data_point_radius = 4,
    data_point_stroke_width = 4,
    data_point_stroke_color = "black",
    data_point_fill_color = "white",
    data_line_stroke_width = 4,
    data_line_stroke_color = "gray",
    show_data_line = TRUE,
    show_data_points = TRUE,
    show_data_area = FALSE
  )

# gt has no fmt_nanoplot(): cols_nanoplot() makes a plot from columns, one value in each
gibraltar_mini <-
  gibraltar |>
  filter(date <= "2023-05-10") |>
  mutate(humidity = humidity * 100) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  mutate(i = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(date, i, temp, humidity) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = i, values_from = c(temp, humidity)) |>
  arrange(date)

gibraltar_mini |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Meteorological Summary of Gibraltar Station",
    subtitle = "Data taken from May 1-10, 2023."
  ) |>
  cols_nanoplot(
    columns = starts_with("temp_"), new_col_name = "temp", autoscale = TRUE,
    options = nano_opts
  ) |>
  cols_nanoplot(
    columns = starts_with("humidity_"), new_col_name = "humidity", autoscale = TRUE,
    options = nano_opts
  ) |>
  fmt_date(columns = date, date_style = "wd_m_day_year") |>
  cols_label(
    date = "Date",
    temp = "Temperature, {{:degree:C}}",
    humidity = "Humidity, % (RH)"
  ) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = c(temp, humidity))
